description:
FOUND s473t6c (#1501 ROUND 10).

t/op/die_unwind.t's rows are
  * "$@ false at start of 'end' block inside 'eval' block"
  * "true value assigned to $@ before 'end' block inside 'eval' block"
  * two `is($uerr, "t3\n")` rows (unnamed, lines 55 and 68)
  * "package Foo; sub DESTROY { die ... }"

s473t6b's #1878 established the entry rule (perl's CLEAR_ERRSV: $@ is cleared
on the way INTO an eval) and the bare-`die` reuse rule.  These rows are the
NEXT layer: what $@ holds while an END block or a DESTROY runs INSIDE an eval
that is already unwinding, and what a die inside that leaves for the outer
eval.

Probe each row standalone against perl before designing anything -- #1878's
own negatives are what found its entry clear, and this file is the same shape
one level deeper.  The last row also needs NS:`DESTROY` called by garbage
collector, so it may not be reachable.
subject: $@ at the START of an eval block that an END or a DESTROY re-enters, and the value a nested die leaves (op/die_unwind.t, 5 rows)
